files.purpose: Top-level window content for Droppy Code: lays out the sidebar column beside the detail pane inside the window's rounded glass chrome, hosts the floating sidebar panel, genie/row-glide overlays, command palette, folder/file drag-and-drop and the global alert; also defines DetailView with its AppKit-backed ThreadColumns chat-column cache, the empty-state WelcomeView with its provider checklist, CopyCommandButton and NoThreadView.

side_effects: handleDrop: FileManager.default.fileExists(atPath:isDirectory:) probes each dropped URL; creates projects via model.addProject(at:) for every dropped folder and a new thread in the last one; attaches dropped files to the selected thread's draft via Storage.attach

DetailView .task(id: threadID): Task.sleep 1500 ms, then polls CGEventSource.secondsSinceLastEventType(.combinedSessionState, eventType: anyInput) with 300 ms sleeps while user input is under 1 second old, and sleeps 400 ms between prebuilds; reads global input-event timing from Quartz

ThreadColumns.Coordinator.prebuild: builds an offscreen SwiftUI hosting view and forces layoutSubtreeIfNeeded(); measures the build with ContinuousClock and logs via SwitchLatency.note("prebuilt <title prefix 24> in <duration>")
ThreadColumns.Coordinator.drop: defers removeFromSuperview behind a 500 ms Task
CopyCommandButton: writes to NSPasteboard.general (clearContents + setString forType .string) and starts a 1.4 second Task to reset the label
OpenProvidersSettingsButton: opens the Settings window (WindowManager.shared.showSettings()) and sets SettingsNavigation.shared.requestedPage = .providers
ProviderStatusRow Login button: Workspace.openTerminal(running: provider.loginCommand) launches Terminal with the provider's sign-in command
Install link opens provider.installURL in the browser

feature_notes: Sidebar modes: onlyFloats = settings.sidebarFloats && settings.sidebarOnlyFloats collapses the sidebar column to width 0 entirely; floats = settings.sidebarFloats && (onlyFloats || !sidebar.isVisible) shows the FloatingSidebarPanel over the chat instead of the toolbar popover. FloatingSidebarPanel receives canClose: !onlyFloats, so in only-floating mode it cannot be dismissed.

Sidebar rows are laid out once at sidebar.width and the slide animates only the outer clip frame (renderedWidth), so rows do not re-wrap per frame; sidebar.noteLaidOutWidth is fed from onGeometryChange of the inner width.

The detail pane is .clipped() deliberately: ReserveSlide offsets carrying a conversation sideways, panels settling after a pane resize, and rows re-wrapping in a live resize otherwise drew over the sidebar or past the window edge for a few frames.
Leading padding on the detail pane is 0 when the sidebar is visible and not only-floating, otherwise Chrome.sheetInset; trailing and vertical padding are always Chrome.sheetInset.

The backdrop is painted first and the whole stack is then clipped to RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: Chrome.windowCornerRadius, style: .continuous), so the glass and its edge stop at the window's own curve.
A coordinate space named GenieAnimator.coordinateSpace is established at the root and used by the GenieLayer and RowGlideLayer overlays.

Drag and drop anywhere in the window (dropDestination for URL.self): directories become projects (one model.addProject per folder), a new thread opens in the last added project, and plain files are attached to the selected thread's draft via Storage.attach(files.map(AttachmentSource.file), to: ...draft.attachments); URLs that do not exist on disk are skipped; handleDrop returns true only if at least one folder or file was accepted.
Alerts are a single OK button with role .cancel, driven by model.alert being non-nil; dismissing writes model.alert = nil.

Chat columns are cached AppKit hosting views, not rebuilt SwiftUI subtrees: Coordinator.keptLimit = 8 columns stay built behind the shown one (while order.count > keptLimit + 1, drop order[0]), because rebuilding a long thread's rows cost about a quarter of a second each switch.

Hidden columns keep the frame they were built at and autoresizingMask [], so a sidebar slide or live resize does not relayout them; the shown column takes pane.bounds with autoresizingMask [.width, .height] and isHidden = false.

show(_:) is a no-op when the id is already shown; otherwise the previous column is hidden, its autoresizingMask cleared and its rootView rebuilt with isShown: false before the new one is revealed or made.

Columns are dropped in dropHidden when their thread has a turn running (the running set), the thread no longer exists (model.thread == nil) or there is no existing runtime, so a hidden column never streams rows unseen at full cost.

Prebuild policy in DetailView: after selecting a thread wait 1500 ms, then build model.neighbors(of: threadID) one at a time; on the first pass of a launch also append the first ThreadColumns.topRowsBuiltAtLaunch = 6 of model.sidebarThreads. Before each build it waits while the last input event is younger than 1 second, polling every 300 ms, and returns entirely if the selected thread starts running; 400 ms between builds.
A prebuilt column is inserted at order index 0 so it is the first evicted, ahead of the columns the reader actually visited.
requested = Set(ids) after each prebuild pass, so a column dropped to make room is not rebuilt on every SwiftUI update.

Dropped columns go into retired and are removed from their superview by a Task 500 ms later, keeping teardown off the switch frame; the retirement Task is cancelled and restarted by each drop and guards on !Task.isCancelled.

Each column's root view is AnyView(ChatView(runtime: model.runtime(for: id)).environment(\.chatColumnIsShown, isShown).modifier(HostedEnvironment(model: model, liveResize: liveResize))); the chatColumnIsShown environment value (default true) is how a view inside a column learns whether it is the visible one, replacing onAppear/onDisappear which would fire for hidden columns.
Columns are hidden rather than detached because a hosting view removed from the window looks disappeared to its views and every task in the column restarts when it returns.
SwitchLatency.note logs "prebuilt <first 24 characters of the thread title, or ?> in <ContinuousClock duration>" for each prebuild.

The Welcome empty state appears only when model.projects.isEmpty; with projects but no selected thread, NoThreadView shows instead. The same branch also runs when the selected thread id no longer resolves to a thread.
NoThreadView reads the live New Thread chord from ShortcutStore.label(for: .newThread) so a remapped shortcut never leaves a stale key on screen; the label is simply omitted when nil.

Provider rows: API-key-based providers never show Install or Login; both the not-installed and the signed-out case show "Add key", which opens Settings and navigates to the Providers page rather than sending the reader to a web page.

CopyCommandButton shows the command text itself and flips to a checkmark plus "Copied" for 1.4 seconds before reverting, matching the transcript's copy button; it previously stayed on "Copied" for the rest of the launch.
unresolved_questions: CopyCommandButton is declared here as an internal (non-private) struct but has no call site inside this file; whether another view still instantiates it, or it is now dead code, cannot be determined from this file alone.
ProviderChecklist declares @Environment(AppModel.self) private var model but never reads it in its body, so it is an unused dependency here (harmless, but likely leftover).

Exact numeric values of Chrome.sheetInset, Chrome.windowCornerRadius, Chrome.trafficLightTop, Chrome.trafficLightDiameter, Chrome.rowButtonLabelHeight and SidebarResizeHandle.hitWidth, and the curve behind Chrome.panelSlide, are defined elsewhere and are not visible in this file.
Whether FrameHostingView subclasses NSHostingView, and how assigning its rootView behaves for a hidden column, is defined in another file.
ActivityThreadStyle has at least a .icon case; the full case list and the exact title/detail strings shown in the Welcome picker live in another file.
sidebar.holdsTrafficLights is passed to WindowChromeConfigurator as sidebarVisible, but the difference between holdsTrafficLights and isVisible is defined in the sidebar model, not here.
